input.plan:
# CLIENT workflow and clone manifests

## What is true today

`mode` is read once in [`app/routes/shared.py`](app/routes/shared.py) (`CLIENT` unless config says `SERVER`). It is not passed to JavaScript.

| Intended CLIENT behavior | Actual code |
|---|---|
| Play local only | Local HTML5 is the default because `stream_mode` is `local`, on both modes. Cast still works if someone connects a device. |
| Hide Chromecast | Bottom transport bar is SERVER-only in [`app/templates/index.html`](app/templates/index.html). Cast icon, menu, discovery thread, and [`app/routes/cast_routes.py`](app/routes/cast_routes.py) stay active on CLIENT. |
| Clone from the server on scan when the server is reachable | Scan in CLIENT calls [`content_transfer.query_server()`](app/utils/content_transfer.py) after the first disk pass ([`backend_handler.py`](app/utils/backend_handler.py)). It always targets configured `server_url`, pulls every DB-missing MP4 (plus images), and has no per-client record. A failed pull still reports “Scan complete (synced from server)” because the return value is ignored. |

There is no client id, registry, or manifest. Handshake tokens are shared secrets, not device identity.

Confirmed product rules for the new sync:

- With no saved manifest, a CLIENT scan downloads nothing (it may still register and upload its catalog if the server answers).
- Skip the pull unless `server_url` answers. Ethernet to that URL counts; do not check a Wi-Fi interface.

## CLIENT: local playback, no cast

- In [`app/templates/top_navbar.html`](app/templates/top_navbar.html), render the cast chip and `#chromecast_menu` only when `system_mode == "SERVER"`.
- In [`app/static/js/app_main.js`](app/static/js/app_main.js), call `getChromecastList` only when that menu exists.
- Do not start `ChromecastHandler` when mode is CLIENT ([`BackEndHandler.get_chromecast`](app/utils/backend_handler.py)). Read mode inside the backend (same config check as `shared.py`) so `shared` → `backend_handler` does not gain a cycle.
- Cast routes return 404 in CLIENT mode. `play_media` keeps resolving `local_play_url` and does not call cast when the handler is absent.
- Local config and [`tests/pytest_mocks.py`](tests/pytest_mocks.py) stay `mode: SERVER`, so existing cast tests keep a handler.

## Sync: reachability, identity, manifest-scoped pull

Extend the CLIENT scan path; do not add a second sync trigger.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    Client->>Server: POST /server_connect client_id plus secret
    alt Unreachable
        Server-->>Client: timeout
        Note over Client: Local scan only
    else Reachable
        Server-->>Client: token plus empty or saved manifest
        Client->>Server: POST inventory of local content_src
        Client->>Client: Delete manifest.remove under media roots
        Client->>Server: Download manifest.clone files only
    end
```

- **Identity:** `client_name` in `app/config.json` if set, otherwise `socket.gethostname()`, sanitized to a filename (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`).
- **Reachability:** existing `server_request` timeout. Connect failure returns `{status: "skipped"}`. [`start_scan_media_directories`](app/utils/backend_handler.py) stores that message on `last_scan_result` (local scan still finishes; second pass still runs so deletions/new files are cataloged when a sync did run).
- **No manifest / empty `clone`:** register the client, store inventory, download zero files. This replaces “pull every missing MP4”.
- **Downloads:** only `clone` entries, by `content_src` (lookup on the server; ids differ per database). Pull cover images only for those entries. Keep the 2GB cap and MD5 check.
- **Removals:** `remove` entries are deleted on the client only when the resolved path is under a configured media root, then dropped from the manifest’s pending remove list after a successful delete report. A path in both lists is a removal (the page will not save that overlap). Order on the client: delete, then download.

Manifest directory: `var/clone_manifests/<client_id>.json` (gitignored). One current file per client, not a new SQLite table and no `DBConnection.VERSION` bump.

```json
{
  "client_id": "living-room-pi",
  "display_name": "Living Room Pi",
  "last_seen": "2026-11-13T15:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-13T14:00:00Z",
  "inventory": [{"content_src": "movies/Title (2010).mp4"}],
  "clone": [{"content_src": "tv_shows/Show - s01e01.mp4"}],
  "remove": []
}
```

**Active** means `last_seen` within 15 minutes (a scan session). **Historical** means any older manifest file. No heartbeat thread.

## SERVER page (transfer-client layout)

New gear-menu item **Clone**, SERVER-only, same pattern as Editor (`get_media_content_types` adds the URL; [`setNavbarLinks`](app/static/js/app_main.js) unhides it).

New template [`app/templates/clone.html`](app/templates/clone.html) plus [`app/static/js/clone.js`](app/static/js/clone.js) (page-local script, not part of the global load order). Bootstrap, no bundler. Layout matches a classic two-pane transfer client:

- Header: client `<select>` grouped into Active and Historical, plus last seen and last manifest save time.
- Left pane: this server’s catalog (`content_src`, title), filter box, multi-select.
- Right pane: that client’s last reported inventory (stale if offline; show the timestamp).
- Actions: **Add to clone**, **Remove from client** (frees space on the next sync), **Save manifest**.

Endpoints (new `APIEndpoints` in [`shared.py`](app/routes/shared.py), handlers in [`transfer_routes.py`](app/routes/transfer_routes.py) or a small `clone_routes.py` imported from [`app/routes/__init__.py`](app/routes/__init__.py)):

- `GET /clone` — page, SERVER only
- `GET /clone/clients` — active and historical list
- `GET /clone/catalog` — server media rows
- `GET /clone/clients/<id>` — manifest + inventory
- `POST /clone/clients/<id>` — replace `clone` and `remove` (JSON). UI-only; handshake is not required on loopback LAN, matching the rest of the app (no Flask auth).

Client-facing additions stay on the existing handshake:

- `POST /server_connect` accepts `client_id` / `display_name`, upserts the file, returns the manifest
- `POST /client_inventory` stores `inventory` and refreshes `last_seen`

`request_content` gains a `content_src` lookup so the client can fetch a manifest entry without a local id. Paths still have to sit under media roots.

## Tests and docs

Unit tests in [`tests/test_content_transfer_unit.py`](tests/test_content_transfer_unit.py) (temp manifest dir, mocked HTTP):

- Unreachable `server_url` → skipped, no download
- Connect with inventory and an empty manifest → zero downloads, file created
- Manifest `clone` of one `content_src` → only that file requested
- `remove` deletes an in-root file and refuses a path outside media roots
- CLIENT cast route / handler start stays off when mode is patched to CLIENT

README: CLIENT plays local and does not cast; scan pulls only the saved manifest when `server_url` answers; Clone page and `var/clone_manifests/` described. Mention backing up that directory the same way as `media_metadata.db` if the manifests matter.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -m "not integration" -q`
- SERVER: open `/clone`, select a client (or the empty state), save a one-title manifest, reload and confirm the selection stuck.
- CLIENT config (or a rendered `index.html` with `system_mode=CLIENT`): no cast control in the top nav; gear menu has no Clone link.

SERVER /clone dual-pane page: active/historical clients, catalog, save clone and remove lists
Unit tests for sync/manifest/cast gate; README note; browser check of /clone and CLIENT nav

The clone page now treats TV the way the catalog already stores it: a show contains seasons, and a season contains episodes.

- Checking a **show** clones every episode in that show. A later scan expands the show again, so new episodes are included.
- Checking a **season** clones only that season’s episodes.
- Checking an **episode** clones that file only. Movies and books stay single rows.
- **Remove from client** targets one episode inside a show or season. That episode is deleted on the next sync and stored as an exclude, so the parent show or season selection does not copy it back.
- The **show cover** is cloned whenever any episode of that show is cloned. A movie or book brings its own cover. The show cover is removed only when no episodes of that show remain on the client.

The plan still assumes several product choices you have not signed off on. These six are independent, so they can be settled together. Reply with the question number and your choice (or “all recommended”).

❓ **Q1** - **Show membership over time**: When a manifest selects a TV show, what should the next scan clone after the show gains a new episode?

- **A.** Re-expand the show on every sync, so new episodes clone automatically. A season selection does the same for that season only.
- **B.** Freeze the episode list at the moment you save. New episodes stay on the server until you edit the manifest.

➡️ **A.** The selection you save is “this show” or “this season,” and a later scan should still mean that.

---

❓ **Q2** - **An episode you removed**: You select a whole show, then remove one episode from the client to free space. On the next successful sync, what happens to that episode?

- **A.** It stays off the client. The show selection remains, with that episode excluded, until you explicitly add it again.
- **B.** It is downloaded again, because the show is still selected.

➡️ **A.** A removal is pointless if the next scan puts the file back.

---

❓ **Q3** - **Which covers travel**: Which images are part of a clone?

- **A.** The show poster whenever any episode of that show is cloned. A movie or book includes its own cover. Season posters and episode stills are not cloned.
- **B.** The show poster only when the whole show is selected. A single episode or a single season clones video only.
- **C.** Clone every image the scanner knows: show poster, season poster, and episode stills.

➡️ **A.** The library poster is the show, movie, or book cover. Episode stills are optional art, not required to play.

---

❓ **Q4** - **When a removal actually deletes the file**: The client only pulls from the server. It does not listen for a push.

- **A.** **Remove from client** queues the delete. The file is removed on the next scan that can reach the server.
- **B.** Removal is refused unless that client is in the middle of a sync right now.

➡️ **A.** You can plan freespace while the mobile server is away, and it applies the next time it is on the network.

---

❓ **Q5** - **What “historical” keeps**: Each client has one manifest file.

- **A.** The file stores the current selections, excludes, removals, last-seen time, and the last inventory the client reported. Older clients remain in the list after they go quiet. Past edits are overwritten on save.
- **B.** Also append a log of every save (what changed, and when) and show that log on the page.

➡️ **A.** One file is enough to restore the choice on the next connection. A change log is a second feature.

---

❓ **Q6** - **How a client is named**: The server has to tell two devices apart the first time each one connects.

- **A.** Use `client_name` from that device’s config if it is set; otherwise use its hostname. The clone page lists that name and lets you see active (seen in the last 15 minutes) versus older clients.
- **B.** The first time a device connects it shows up as a hostname, and you must rename it on the server before you can save a manifest.

➡️ **A.** A name in config is stable even if the hostname changes, and you can still save a manifest before anyone renames it.
